title: How many loaves does the baker bake in six weeks?
description: A baker bakes fourteen loaves every day except Sunday. The loaves in six weeks are written in two ways, by counting the open days and by taking the shut days from all the days. Keeko doubts that all seven days count.
teaching_notes: One idea: the open days are all the days minus the shut days, so the same loaf count is written two ways. Watch for students who count every day of the week, including the shut day.

source: A baker bakes 14 loaves every day except Sunday. Write expressions for the loaves in 6 weeks in two ways and find the value.
video_script.why: A learner sees that a count of open days can be written two ways with brackets and that both ways agree.
video_script.substitution: Replace fourteen loaves, one shut day and six weeks with any daily amount, any number of shut days and any number of weeks.
video_script.anchor: a baker who bakes fourteen loaves each day for six weeks, with Sunday shut
video_script.wrong_answer: the loaves are seven times six times fourteen using all the days
video_script.wrong_move: counts all 7 days of every week as baking days, so the shut Sunday is baked as well
video_script.payoff_line: The baker bakes five hundred and four loaves in six weeks.

final_answer.spoken: the baker bakes five hundred and four loaves in six weeks

video_script.design: A calendar of six weeks with the Sunday of every week crossed out. The open days are counted, and then all days are counted and the shut days are taken away.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; a baker beside a tray of 14 loaves and a calendar week with Sunday crossed out

marks.h2: a baker and a tray of fourteen loaves appear
marks.h3: a week appears with Sunday crossed out

narration: <bookmark mark='h1'/>This is a question from your book about a baker.
<bookmark mark='h2'/>The baker bakes fourteen loaves every day except Sunday.
<bookmark mark='h3'/>The bakery is shut on Sunday.
<bookmark mark='h4'/>How many loaves does the baker bake in six weeks?

beats.on_screen: the baker and the week stay on the board and the question mark keeps glowing

marks.t1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='t1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a row of 7 days with the Sunday cell crossed out, leaving 6 open days

marks.g1: the seven day cells of a week are drawn
marks.g2: the Sunday cell is crossed out
marks.g3: the six open cells are marked with loaves

beats.colours: the shut day in a second colour
narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A week has seven days, and the bakery is shut on one of them.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>Only the open days have loaves.
<bookmark mark='g3'/>We can count the open days, or count all the days and take away the shut ones.

beats.on_screen: Given: 14 loaves every day except Sunday; 6 weeks

marks.gv1: the loaves and the weeks are written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, fourteen loaves every day except Sunday, for six weeks.

beats.on_screen: To find: the loaves in 6 weeks, written in two ways, and the value

marks.fd1: the words two ways and the value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='fd1'/>We have to write the loaves in two ways and find the value.

beats.on_screen: open days in a week: 7 − 1 = 6; open days in 6 weeks: (7 − 1) × 6 = 36

marks.s12: (7 − 1) × 6 is written, and the value 36 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='s11'/>Step one, count the open days.
A week has seven days, and one is shut, so seven minus one days are open.
<bookmark mark='s12'/>In six weeks, the open days are open bracket seven minus one close bracket times six. That is thirty six.

marks.s21: 14 loaves are put on each of the open days

narration: <bookmark mark='s21'/>Step two, way one.
Each open day has fourteen loaves.
<bookmark mark='s22'/>The loaves are open bracket seven minus one close bracket times six times fourteen. That is thirty six times fourteen.

beats.on_screen: way two: all days 7 × 6 × 14 = 588; shut days 1 × 6 × 14 = 84; 588 − 84

marks.s31: all the days are counted first and 588 appears
marks.s32: the shut days are counted and 84 appears

narration: <bookmark mark='s31'/>Step three, way two.
Count all the days first, which is seven times six times fourteen, or five hundred and eighty eight.
<bookmark mark='s32'/>Then count the shut days, which is one times six times fourteen, or eighty four.
<bookmark mark='s33'/>Take the shut days from all the days to get five hundred and eighty eight minus eighty four.

marks.s41: the bracket of way one is opened
marks.s42: the opened form meets way two

narration: <bookmark mark='s41'/>Step four, join the two ways.
Opening the bracket in way one gives seven times six times fourteen minus one times six times fourteen.
<bookmark mark='s42'/>This is exactly way two.
<bookmark mark='a1'/>The baker bakes five hundred and four loaves in six weeks.
Both ways give the same number of loaves.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the board
narration: <bookmark mark='k1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble: 7 × 6 × 14, using all the days; it is struck out and the crossed Sunday cells are shown

marks.k3: the six crossed Sunday cells light up

narration: <bookmark mark='k2'/>Keeko thinks the loaves are seven times six times fourteen using all the days.
<bookmark mark='k3'/>But Sunday has no baking at all.
<bookmark mark='k4'/>The shut days must come out.
